cards.explanation: The answer is that the bones are very dry. Ezekiel says he saw a great many bones on the valley floor, "…and indeed, they were very dry." (Ezekiel 37:2) The LORD led him all around among them, so he got a close look. Hold onto that picture, friends, because it matters for what comes next.

The LORD asks, "Son of man, can these bones come to life?" (Ezekiel 37:3) "Son of man…" is how He addresses Ezekiel here. Of all the things He could ask in a valley full of dry bones, friends, He asks that one. It sets up the whole scene.

The answer is False. Ezekiel never says it could never happen. He replies, "O Lord GOD, only You know." (Ezekiel 37:3) No yes, no no, just handing the question back to the One who can answer it. Honestly, friends, I'd have blurted out something way less wise.

The answer is breath. The Lord GOD says, "I will cause breath to enter you, and you will come to life." (Ezekiel 37:5) Notice who's doing the work, friends: He says "I will." The bones don't have to do a thing but listen.

The answer is that they will know He is the LORD. After the tendons, flesh, skin and breath, God says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 37:6) The whole promise ends with them knowing who He is. Not a bad takeaway from a valley of bones, bakers.

The answer is rattling! Ezekiel says, "…there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone." (Ezekiel 37:7) Picture a whole valley of bones clacking into place. That's one sound I'd stop everything to hear, friends.

The answer is True. Ezekiel says the bones "…came together, bone to bone." (Ezekiel 37:7) This happens as he prophesies, just as he was commanded. The valley goes from scattered bones to bones joined up, friends.

The answer is False. Ezekiel sees tendons, flesh and skin, "but there was no breath in them." (Ezekiel 37:8) So they have the look of bodies, but no breathing yet. That missing breath is the detail to hold onto, friends.

The answer is the four winds. God tells Ezekiel to say, "Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!" (Ezekiel 37:9) That's breath called in from every direction, friends. Nobody's left out of the call.

The answer is True. Ezekiel says, "…the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood on their feet…" (Ezekiel 37:10) The bodies that were lying still are up and standing. The breath was the missing piece, bakers.
The answer is a vast army. Ezekiel says they came to life and stood on their feet, "…a vast army." (Ezekiel 37:10) The valley had been full of bones, friends. Now it's a whole army standing up.

The answer is their hope. The people say, "Our bones are dried up, and our hope has perished; we are cut off." (Ezekiel 37:11) Those are heavy words, friends. I think that's a hard place to be, and God doesn't skip over it. He takes their own words and answers them.

The answer is their graves. God says, "O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them…" (Ezekiel 37:12) He says "My people," so these are His own. Opening graves is a big promise, friends, and He says it again in verse 13.

The answer is True. God says, "…I will bring you back to the land of Israel." (Ezekiel 37:12) That promise comes right alongside opening the graves. He's not just lifting them up, friends, He's bringing them home.

The answer is Spirit. God says, "I will put My Spirit in you and you will live…" (Ezekiel 37:14) The same verse says He'll settle them in their own land. That's a promise straight from His own mouth, bakers.

The answer is False. Nothing is left open. God says, "Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD." (Ezekiel 37:14) He doesn't just speak, friends. He says He will do it, and that's the last word on it.
